column2: It is Geheimnisnacht, the night of mystery, when even the bravest peasants bar their doors. The lords of Sylvania have been summoned to Drakenhof for a ball. The hall is lit by black candles and the music never stops. At midnight the doors are barred and Vlad von Carstein rises from his throne, no longer bothering to hide what he is. He walks among his guests and offers each the same gift: eternal life in his service. Those who refuse will have made an enemy who never dies.
Bare my throat for the Blood Kiss.
I will serve you living, my lord.
Never. I will not be one of you.

The Geheimnisnacht Ball is over. The black candles have burned down and the musicians lie drained in the gallery. One by one the living lords of Sylvania knelt before you: most took the Blood Kiss, some swore to serve you living, and the few who refused rode home through the dark with your name on their lips. Sylvania is yours, body and soul.
Let the Empire hear of it.

You break the seals of a barrow older than the Empire and speak the words of binding into the dark. Something stirs on the bier: a champion of a forgotten tribe, still in his rusted mail. Cold light kindles in his empty sockets as he rises and lifts his blade in salute. He will lead your dead without rest or fear for as long as your will holds him.

You break the seals of a great barrow and speak the words of binding, and the dead who answer are not one but many: a king's household, laid around their lord. The king himself rises last, a crown of tarnished bronze on his skull and a nightmare stamping in the dark behind him. He kneels to the one who woke him. A Wight King serves you now.

[From.GetFirstName] the wight is gone. When the will that bound [From.GetFirstName] to the world was gone, there was nothing left to hold the bones together, and [From.GetFirstName] fell into dust and rust before the court. The servants swept what was left out of the hall.

You have a fine piece of war gear that could be made far deadlier, if it were bound with the magic of death. Such work needs a necromancer of great power. You could work it yourself if your power is great enough, pay a necromancer of your realm, or seek out one of the Necrarchs, who ask much more but never fail.
I will work the enchantment myself.
[undead_enchanter_necromancer.GetTitledFirstName] will do it, for a fee.
The circle is drawn in grave dirt and the candles are made from the fat of hanged men. Everything is ready for the binding. Which piece will you bind?
[undead_enchanter_necromancer.GetFirstName] has gathered what the ritual needs: grave dirt, a murderer's bones and a great deal of your silver. All that is left is to choose which piece to bind.

In a tower that smells of old blood and ink, [undead_enchanter_necrarch.GetFirstName] has made everything ready. The Necrarch is impatient for the work to start, and is willing to bind whichever piece you bring.
I no longer have anything worth binding.
The candles gutter and go out, and when they are lit again the old piece is gone. In its place lies something cold and dark that seems to drink the light. It is yours.
At the height of the ritual the circle breaks and the spirits scatter with a scream. When the smoke clears your piece lies untouched in the dirt, unchanged. The silver and the effort are lost.

Break open an old barrow and bind its champion back into his bones. A wight leads your armies without rest or fear, but only while a master of the dead holds his leash. One barrow in twenty holds a king.
Has not raised a wight in the last ten years
Has fewer than three wights at court
Have a fine weapon or suit of armour bound with the magic of death. The old piece becomes a necromantic one of its kind.
Has a fine weapon or armour that is not necromantic already
A barrow lord of old, raised to lead the dead once more.
This character has raised a wight recently.
A dead champion bound back into his bones by a vampire or a necromancer. A wight knows no fear and no rest, but when his master's will is gone he falls back into dust.
fell back into dust when the will that bound the bones was gone
The blade a barrow king was buried with. It has lain in the dark beside him for a thousand years and thirsts for the light of battle.
This blade of blue ice-steel is bound with spells so deadly that its merest touch sucks the soul from its victim and freezes his heart.
An accursed and ageless blade that thirsts for the souls of its enemies.
A headsman's axe of black iron that never dulls, however many necks it parts.
The Dreadlance is uncannily accurate, said to find its target even in the dark of night.
The lance of a knight who never stopped riding. It thirsts for the souls of its enemies.
A drowned captain's cutlass, still dripping. No kind or just hand can hold it.
Black wood from the wrecks off Sartosa, harder than steel and bound with the curse of the Vampire Coast.
This blade drips with brine and is covered in rust, but it slices through the thickest armour.
A cage of enchanted gold that guards the vampire's exposed heart.
A product of ancient and twisted sorcery, this construct of bone offers great protection to undead wizards.
This crimson armour makes its wearer look disturbingly like a walking, flayed cadaver. No Lahmian or Necrarch will wear it.
A coat of mail that never stops weeping blood.
The black-enamelled Armour of Night wraps its wearer in an impenetrable cloud of darkness. Only those who fight on foot can wear it.
Heavy, ageless plate that will not let its wearer flee the field. Only those who fight on foot can wear it.
The salt-stained finery of a living pirate captain who sails for the dead.
The sea-rotted coat of an admiral of the Vampire Coast, heavy with brine and old gold braid.
Made of interlocking tentacles and seashells and forever dripping slime, this armour clings to its wearer like a second skin. Only those who fight on foot can wear it.
A glistening coat of Merwyrm scales, enchanted to stay wet forever. Only those who fight on foot can wear it.

The living of a vampire's realm pay their lord in blood: a son or daughter given up from every family or village, to be drained. How much each community must give depends on the vampire who rules the land. Light taxes please mortal vassals and starve the vampire ones. Heavy taxes fill the levies with the drained and the raised, and stir up revolt.
Only the condemned and those who offer themselves are bled.
A few each year from the gaols and the poorest villages, and most of them come home.
Every village gives its share each year, and not all of them come back. The drained swell the levies.
Twice a year the tithe-takers come, and they take by force if they must.
Every community bleeds whenever its lord is thirsty, on pain of death.
